title: Median vs average movement value
q: Averages hide outliers. For each MovementCategory, show MovementCategory, StockMovements (how many stock movements), AverageValue, MedianValue and AboveMedian (AverageValue minus MedianValue), all money values rounded to 2 decimals. Use the MovementValue column. Sort by MovementCategory.
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT MovementCategory,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY MovementCategory) AS StockMovements,
           AVG(MovementValue) OVER (PARTITION BY MovementCategory) AS AvgV,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY MovementValue) OVER (PARTITION BY MovementCategory) AS MedV
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements
)
SELECT MovementCategory, StockMovements,
       CAST(AvgV AS decimal(12,2)) AS AverageValue,
       CAST(MedV AS decimal(12,2)) AS MedianValue,
       CAST(AvgV - MedV AS decimal(12,2)) AS AboveMedian
FROM m
ORDER BY MovementCategory;
how: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) returns the median on every row of the group; SELECT DISTINCT collapses it to one row per group. When the median is far below the average, a few large values pull the average up.
a:
**Approach hint:** PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) returns the median on every row of the group; SELECT DISTINCT collapses it to one row per group. When the median is far below the average, a few large values pull the average up.

| B | 100 | 309.92 | 273.77 | 36.15 |
| C | 40 | 900.58 | 747.42 | 153.16 |

title: Month-to-date running total
q: For Closed stock movements only, show each MovementDate with DayTotal (the sum of MovementValue that day) and MonthToDate: the running total that starts again on the first day of each month. Sort by MovementDate.
sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT MovementDate, SUM(MovementValue) AS DayTotal
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements
    WHERE Status = 'Closed'
    GROUP BY MovementDate
)
SELECT MovementDate, DayTotal,
       SUM(DayTotal) OVER (PARTITION BY YEAR(MovementDate), MONTH(MovementDate)
                           ORDER BY MovementDate ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS MonthToDate
FROM d
ORDER BY MovementDate;
how: Aggregate to one row per day first, then SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY year and month ORDER BY date). The PARTITION BY is what makes the total restart each month.
a:
**Approach hint:** Aggregate to one row per day first, then SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY year and month ORDER BY date). The PARTITION BY is what makes the total restart each month.

title: Peak stock level per warehouse
q: A warehouse's stock level starts at the sum of its OpeningQuantity in StockBalances. Apply its Closed movements in MovedAt order (IN adds MovedUnits, OUT subtracts). For each warehouse with movements, show WarehouseName, Opening, PeakLevel (highest level reached after any movement), PeakAt (MovedAt of the first time it reached that peak) and EndLevel (level after its last movement). Show the 10 warehouses with the highest PeakLevel (ties by WarehouseName). Sort by PeakLevel descending, then WarehouseName.
sql:
WITH o AS (
    SELECT WarehouseID, SUM(OpeningQuantity) AS Opening
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockBalances
    GROUP BY WarehouseID
), r AS (
    SELECT m.WarehouseID, m.MovedAt, m.MovementID, o.Opening,
           o.Opening + SUM(CASE WHEN m.Direction = 'IN' THEN m.MovedUnits ELSE -m.MovedUnits END)
               OVER (PARTITION BY m.WarehouseID ORDER BY m.MovedAt, m.MovementID ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS Level
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements AS m
    JOIN o ON o.WarehouseID = m.WarehouseID
    WHERE m.Status = 'Closed'
), s AS (
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY WarehouseID ORDER BY Level DESC, MovedAt, MovementID) AS PeakN,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY WarehouseID ORDER BY MovedAt DESC, MovementID DESC) AS LastN
    FROM r
), w AS (
    SELECT WarehouseID, MAX(Opening) AS Opening,
           MAX(CASE WHEN PeakN = 1 THEN Level END) AS PeakLevel,
           MAX(CASE WHEN PeakN = 1 THEN MovedAt END) AS PeakAt,
           MAX(CASE WHEN LastN = 1 THEN Level END) AS EndLevel
    FROM s
    GROUP BY WarehouseID
)
SELECT TOP (10) wh.WarehouseName, w.Opening, w.PeakLevel, w.PeakAt, w.EndLevel
FROM w
JOIN retail_supply_chain.Warehouses AS wh ON wh.WarehouseID = w.WarehouseID
ORDER BY w.PeakLevel DESC, wh.WarehouseName;
how: Signed running SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse ORDER BY time) plus the opening stock gives the level after every movement. Then two ROW_NUMBERs pick the peak row and the last row, and MAX(CASE ...) folds them into one row.
a:
**Approach hint:** Signed running SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse ORDER BY time) plus the opening stock gives the level after every movement. Then two ROW_NUMBERs pick the peak row and the last row, and MAX(CASE ...) folds them into one row.

title: Below reorder level, with the source to call
q: List stock balances where QuantityOnHand is below ReorderLevel. For each, show WarehouseName, ProductName, Sourcing, QuantityOnHand, ReorderLevel, Shortfall (ReorderLevel minus QuantityOnHand) and the supplier who delivered that product most often into any warehouse (IN movements; ties go to the shorter LeadTimeDays, then the alphabetically first name) as Supplier and LeadTimeDays. Use NULL when the product has never been delivered. Sort by Shortfall descending, then WarehouseName, ProductName.
sql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT m.ProductID, su.SupplierName, su.LeadTimeDays,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.ProductID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, su.LeadTimeDays, su.SupplierName) AS rn
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements AS m
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Suppliers AS su ON su.SupplierID = m.SupplierID
    WHERE m.Direction = 'IN'
    GROUP BY m.ProductID, su.SupplierID, su.SupplierName, su.LeadTimeDays
)
SELECT w.WarehouseName, p.ProductName, p.Sourcing, b.QuantityOnHand, b.ReorderLevel,
       b.ReorderLevel - b.QuantityOnHand AS Shortfall, s.SupplierName AS Supplier, s.LeadTimeDays
FROM retail_supply_chain.StockBalances AS b
JOIN retail_supply_chain.Warehouses AS w ON w.WarehouseID = b.WarehouseID
JOIN retail_supply_chain.Products AS p ON p.ProductID = b.ProductID
LEFT JOIN s ON s.ProductID = b.ProductID AND s.rn = 1
WHERE b.QuantityOnHand < b.ReorderLevel
ORDER BY Shortfall DESC, w.WarehouseName, p.ProductName;
how: Rank suppliers per product with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (... ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, tie-breakers) right after GROUP BY. Put rn = 1 in the LEFT JOIN condition (not WHERE) so products with no supplier stay.
a:
**Approach hint:** Rank suppliers per product with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (... ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, tie-breakers) right after GROUP BY. Put rn = 1 in the LEFT JOIN condition (not WHERE) so products with no supplier stay.

title: Monthly IN vs OUT, side by side
q: For Closed movements, show one row per month: Month (yyyy-MM), UnitsIn, UnitsOut, NetUnits (in minus out) and CumulativeNet (running NetUnits from the first month). Sort by Month.
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT FORMAT(MovementDate, 'yyyy-MM') AS Month,
           SUM(CASE WHEN Direction = 'IN' THEN MovedUnits ELSE 0 END) AS UnitsIn,
           SUM(CASE WHEN Direction = 'OUT' THEN MovedUnits ELSE 0 END) AS UnitsOut
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements
    WHERE Status = 'Closed'
    GROUP BY FORMAT(MovementDate, 'yyyy-MM')
)
SELECT Month, UnitsIn, UnitsOut, UnitsIn - UnitsOut AS NetUnits,
       SUM(UnitsIn - UnitsOut) OVER (ORDER BY Month ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS CumulativeNet
FROM m
ORDER BY Month;
how: Conditional aggregation (SUM(CASE ...)) pivots IN and OUT into columns; a running SUM() OVER (ORDER BY Month) adds the cumulative column.
a:
**Approach hint:** Conditional aggregation (SUM(CASE ...)) pivots IN and OUT into columns; a running SUM() OVER (ORDER BY Month) adds the cumulative column.

title: Material usage vs the recipe
q: The recipe (BillOfMaterials) says how much of each material one unit of a Made product needs. For Completed production orders, compare actual MaterialUsage with PlannedUnits × QuantityPerUnit for each material in the recipe. List order-material pairs that used more than 3% over plan: ProductionReference, ProductName, MaterialName, Planned, Used and OverPct (2 decimals). Sort by OverPct descending, then ProductionReference, MaterialName.
sql:
WITH u AS (
    SELECT ProductionOrderID, MaterialID, SUM(QuantityUsed) AS Used
    FROM retail_supply_chain.MaterialUsage
    GROUP BY ProductionOrderID, MaterialID
), x AS (
    SELECT po.ProductionReference, p.ProductName, m.MaterialName,
           po.PlannedUnits * b.QuantityPerUnit AS Planned, COALESCE(u.Used, 0) AS Used
    FROM retail_supply_chain.ProductionOrders AS po
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Products AS p ON p.ProductID = po.ProductID
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.BillOfMaterials AS b ON b.ProductID = po.ProductID
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Materials AS m ON m.MaterialID = b.MaterialID
    LEFT JOIN u ON u.ProductionOrderID = po.ProductionOrderID AND u.MaterialID = b.MaterialID
    WHERE po.ProductionStatus = 'Completed'
)
SELECT ProductionReference, ProductName, MaterialName, Planned, Used,
       CAST(100.0 * (Used - Planned) / Planned AS decimal(7,2)) AS OverPct
FROM x
WHERE Used > Planned * 1.03
ORDER BY OverPct DESC, ProductionReference, MaterialName;
how: The plan comes from joining each order to its product's recipe; the actuals are summed per order and material, then LEFT JOINed on both keys.
a:
**Approach hint:** The plan comes from joining each order to its product's recipe; the actuals are summed per order and material, then LEFT JOINed on both keys.

title: Actual material cost vs planned cost, by region
q: Actual cost of a production order is the sum of QuantityUsed × Materials.UnitCost. For Completed orders, show per Region of the receiving warehouse: Orders, PlannedCost (sum), ActualCost (sum, 2 decimals) and OverrunPct ((Actual − Planned) ÷ Planned × 100, 2 decimals). PlannedCost must count each order once. Sort by OverrunPct descending, then Region.
sql:
WITH a AS (
    SELECT mu.ProductionOrderID, SUM(mu.QuantityUsed * m.UnitCost) AS ActualCost
    FROM retail_supply_chain.MaterialUsage AS mu
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Materials AS m ON m.MaterialID = mu.MaterialID
    GROUP BY mu.ProductionOrderID
)
SELECT w.Region, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(po.PlannedCost) AS PlannedCost,
       CAST(SUM(COALESCE(a.ActualCost, 0)) AS decimal(14,2)) AS ActualCost,
       CAST(100.0 * (SUM(COALESCE(a.ActualCost, 0)) - SUM(po.PlannedCost)) / SUM(po.PlannedCost) AS decimal(7,2)) AS OverrunPct
FROM retail_supply_chain.ProductionOrders AS po
JOIN retail_supply_chain.Warehouses AS w ON w.WarehouseID = po.WarehouseID
LEFT JOIN a ON a.ProductionOrderID = po.ProductionOrderID
WHERE po.ProductionStatus = 'Completed'
GROUP BY w.Region
ORDER BY OverrunPct DESC, w.Region;
how: Cost the usage per order first; joining orders straight to usage rows would add PlannedCost once per usage row.
a:
**Approach hint:** Cost the usage per order first; joining orders straight to usage rows would add PlannedCost once per usage row.

title: Factory to shelf: completed but not yet received
q: A Completed production order is *received* when an IN stock movement points to it (StockMovements.ProductionOrderID). For each Region of the receiving warehouse show CompletedOrders, Received, NotReceived, UnitsWaiting (PlannedUnits of the orders not received) and AvgDaysToShelf (average days from CompletedDate to the first receipt's MovementDate, 1 decimal, received orders only). Sort by UnitsWaiting descending, then Region.
sql:
WITH r AS (
    SELECT ProductionOrderID, MIN(MovementDate) AS ReceivedDate
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements
    WHERE ProductionOrderID IS NOT NULL AND Direction = 'IN'
    GROUP BY ProductionOrderID
)
SELECT w.Region,
       COUNT(*) AS CompletedOrders,
       COUNT(r.ProductionOrderID) AS Received,
       COUNT(*) - COUNT(r.ProductionOrderID) AS NotReceived,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.ProductionOrderID IS NULL THEN po.PlannedUnits ELSE 0 END) AS UnitsWaiting,
       CAST(AVG(CAST(DATEDIFF(day, po.CompletedDate, r.ReceivedDate) AS decimal(9,2))) AS decimal(9,1)) AS AvgDaysToShelf
FROM retail_supply_chain.ProductionOrders AS po
JOIN retail_supply_chain.Warehouses AS w ON w.WarehouseID = po.WarehouseID
LEFT JOIN r ON r.ProductionOrderID = po.ProductionOrderID
WHERE po.ProductionStatus = 'Completed'
GROUP BY w.Region
ORDER BY UnitsWaiting DESC, w.Region;
how: Reduce receipts to one row per production order first, then LEFT JOIN so unreceived orders stay. COUNT(column) skips NULLs, so COUNT(*) minus COUNT(r.ProductionOrderID) is the number not received; AVG also ignores the NULL day counts.
a:
**Approach hint:** Reduce receipts to one row per production order first, then LEFT JOIN so unreceived orders stay. COUNT(column) skips NULLs, so COUNT(*) minus COUNT(r.ProductionOrderID) is the number not received; AVG also ignores the NULL day counts.

title: Stock value: bought vs made
q: Value on-hand stock as QuantityOnHand × Products.UnitCost. For each warehouse Region show BoughtValue, MadeValue, TotalValue and MadeSharePct (MadeValue as a percentage of TotalValue, 2 decimals), plus a final row with Region = 'All regions'. Sort the regions by TotalValue descending with the total row last.
sql:
WITH v AS (
    SELECT w.Region,
           SUM(CASE WHEN p.Sourcing = 'Bought' THEN b.QuantityOnHand * p.UnitCost ELSE 0 END) AS BoughtValue,
           SUM(CASE WHEN p.Sourcing = 'Made' THEN b.QuantityOnHand * p.UnitCost ELSE 0 END) AS MadeValue
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockBalances AS b
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Warehouses AS w ON w.WarehouseID = b.WarehouseID
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Products AS p ON p.ProductID = b.ProductID
    GROUP BY ROLLUP (w.Region)
)
SELECT COALESCE(Region, 'All regions') AS Region, BoughtValue, MadeValue, BoughtValue + MadeValue AS TotalValue,
       CAST(100.0 * MadeValue / NULLIF(BoughtValue + MadeValue, 0) AS decimal(5,2)) AS MadeSharePct
FROM v
ORDER BY CASE WHEN Region IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, TotalValue DESC;
how: Conditional aggregation splits Bought and Made into columns. GROUP BY ROLLUP adds the grand-total row (Region is NULL there), and a CASE in ORDER BY pushes that row to the bottom.
a:
**Approach hint:** Conditional aggregation splits Bought and Made into columns. GROUP BY ROLLUP adds the grand-total row (Region is NULL there), and a CASE in ORDER BY pushes that row to the bottom.

title: Longest quiet period per region
q: For each Region (from Warehouses), find the longest stretch with no stock movements at all between two consecutive stock movement dates in that region. Show Region, GapStart (the last date before the gap), GapEnd (the next date) and DaysWithout. If two gaps tie for longest in a region, show both. Sort by DaysWithout descending, then Region, then GapStart.
sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT p.Region, e.MovementDate AS GapEnd,
           LAG(e.MovementDate) OVER (PARTITION BY p.Region ORDER BY e.MovementDate, e.MovementID) AS GapStart
    FROM retail_supply_chain.StockMovements AS e
    JOIN retail_supply_chain.Warehouses AS p ON p.WarehouseID = e.WarehouseID
), r AS (
    SELECT Region, GapStart, GapEnd, DATEDIFF(day, GapStart, GapEnd) AS DaysWithout,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Region ORDER BY DATEDIFF(day, GapStart, GapEnd) DESC) AS rk
    FROM d
    WHERE GapStart IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT Region, GapStart, GapEnd, DaysWithout
FROM r
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY DaysWithout DESC, Region, GapStart;
how: LAG over the region's dates gives the previous date; DATEDIFF gives the gap. RANK() (not ROW_NUMBER) keeps ties for the top spot.
a:
**Approach hint:** LAG over the region's dates gives the previous date; DATEDIFF gives the gap. RANK() (not ROW_NUMBER) keeps ties for the top spot.
